title: Design Regret with Heavy-Tailed Outcomes under Arbitrary versus Randomly Shuffled Arrival Order

gap_reasons: The delivered proofs match the advertised ordered and shuffled rates, including the logarithmic endpoint; the signed depletion term and unrestricted-policy converses are discharged rather than deferred. Novelty rests on the complete-class hidden-permutation frontier, since fourth-moment ordered regret and bounded iid logarithmic tracking are established background in [Sigmoid-FTRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19905v2) and [ClipSMT](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v258/neopane25a.html). proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matching ordinary-HT design-regret orders for adversarial and hidden shuffled arrival on the full finite-population empirical-q class, including the logarithmic endpoint and unrestricted-policy converses. Primary citations were retrieved and attested, and the unused fixed-design proposition was deleted; final math and decision reviews pass without findings. The novelty reviewer grades the result subfield at score ceiling 7.2, below the fixed field floor 7.4; the run therefore stops before formalization, with no Lean proof certificate or substrate promotion.
tldr: For the ordinary untruncated HT causal contrast on a fixed finite roster with empirical \(q\)-moment bounds, the design-only minimax cumulative variance regret is \(\Theta_q(T^{2/q})\) under arbitrary arrival order. An independent hidden shuffle changes it to \(\Theta_q(T^{4/q-1})\) for every fixed \(2<q<4\), and to \(\Theta(\log T)\) at \(q=4\). Explicit policies use only logged raw outcomes, assignments, and propensities, and the lower bounds cover all admissible randomized Borel policies without a common propensity floor. Shuffling therefore gives a strict asymptotic gain for every fixed \(q\in(2,4]\). The benchmark is the best fixed-probability HT variance on the full array; the endpoint logarithmic witnesses already belong to the published bounded-row subclass \(\mathcal B_T\).
gap: Published arbitrary-order moment guarantees and bounded iid tracking leave the cost of hidden random arrival unresolved on the complete empirical \(q\)-moment class.
fill: An evaluated pair of minimax rates, total raw-record allocation algorithms, unrestricted-policy converses, and an explicit arrival-order improvement region quantify this design lever.
